title: Closed exceptional transposes and both composition cocycles
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ and a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E,L/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be finite extensions, $m,n\ge1$, $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^m$, $B=\mathcal O_L/\varpi_L^n$, and $\varphi:A\to B$ any unital map [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. On each scheme $T$ use constant module sheaves on its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and write $S_T^{A,B}K=K_B=K\otimes_A^LB$ for uncompleted derived scalar extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The notation $D^b_{ctf}$ means bounded constructible with finite Tor amplitude [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. All schemes below are separated and finite type over $k$; all scheme maps are $k$-maps [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constructible exceptional functors and their adjunctions on bounded constructible inputs of etale origin [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and ordinary derived direct images [def-weil-derived-direct-image]. For each closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$, suppose the relevant finite-Tor bounded constructible domains are closed under scalar extension and $Ri_R^!$ at every finite coefficient stage $R$ under consideration, and use $i_{*,R}\dashv Ri_R^!$ with counit $\epsilon_{i,R}$. Let $c_i^{A,B}:S_X^{A,B}i_{*,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}i_{*,B}S_Z^{A,B}$ be exactly the ordinary coefficient comparison of [lem-coef-finite-direct-image]. Define $b_i^{A,B}$ as the right mate of $(c_i^{A,B})^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Thus, with $N=Ri_A^!M$,
$$\epsilon_{i,B,S_XM}\,i_{*,B}(b_{i,M}^{A,B})=S_X(\epsilon_{i,A,M})(c_{i,N}^{A,B})^{-1}.$$
The maps $b_i$ are natural in $M$. For closed immersions $W\xrightarrow{t}Z\xrightarrow{i}X$, identify $(it)_*$ with $i_*t_*$ by [lem-weil-derived-direct-image-composition] and $R(it)^!$ with $Rt^!Ri^!$ by the chained Hom adjunction [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], whose counit is $\epsilon_i\circ i_*\epsilon_t$. Then
$$b_{it,M}^{A,B}=Rt_B^!(b_{i,M}^{A,B})\circ b_{t,Ri_A^!M}^{A,B}.$$
For a third finite coefficient stage $C=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^s$ with $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $s\ge1$, and a unital map $B\to C$, the balancing maps $((x\otimes b)\otimes c)\mapsto x\otimes bc$ on flat-term K-flat representatives induce canonical natural identifications $S_T^{B,C}S_T^{A,B}\cong S_T^{A,C}$. Under them,
$$b_{i,M}^{A,C}=b_{i,S_X^{A,B}M}^{B,C}\circ S_Z^{B,C}(b_{i,M}^{A,B}).$$
For identity coefficient change the comparison is the identity. These formulas assert coherence of the specified maps, without assuming that $b_i$ is invertible; they apply whenever all the displayed domains are defined.

Its right-adjoint identifications are definitionally rightComp. proof.text: For closedTranspose_coefficient, prove a private generic mate_chain lemma by injectivity of the C closed-adjunction transpose. Move the final right-adjoint map through its counit, substitute mateEquiv_counit for the B-to-C mate, use naturality of the inverse ordinary comparison at the A-to-B mate, substitute its mateEquiv_counit equation, and finally use naturality of the scalar compositor. Instantiate this lemma with the inverse ordinary comparisons and scalarComp. The required inverse ordinary chain equation is obtained by taking Iso.inv of the ordinary coefficientChain isomorphism equation from step 2.

proof.text: For closedTranspose_identity, first specialize the ordinary coefficient chain law to two identity ring maps. By scalarComp_identity its compositors are the canonical scalar units. For an invertible comparison c:F T -> S F with units s:S ~= Id and t:T ~= Id, this equation reads c_K=t^{-1}_{TFK} T(c_K) c_{SK} F(s_{SK}). Multiply by t_{TFK}, use its naturality and cancel the invertible T(c_K); this gives c_{SK}F(s_{SK})=t_{FSK}. Naturality of c at s_K, naturality of s, and cancellation of T(F(s_K)) give c_K F(s_K)=t_{FK}. Apply this generic proved calculation to the actual comparison. Now transpose the proposed exceptional unit equation under the given closed adjunction, use counit naturality and mateEquiv_counit, move the scalar unit by naturality, and cancel c against c inverse using the ordinary unit equation just proved. Both transposes agree.
